settings.happDesc: Settings delivered exclusively to HAPP clients via HTTP headers on every subscription update.
settings.happAnnounceHint: Short message shown to users inside the app (max 200 characters). Non-ASCII text (e.g. Cyrillic) is encoded automatically.
settings.softBlockDesc: Instead of an error, serve a valid subscription whose servers are fake locations with your message. Works for all apps.
settings.softBlockEnableHint: When off, invalid subscriptions return a plain 403 (legacy behavior).
settings.softBlockRemarkHint: Each non-empty line becomes a separate server name in the client. Shown to all apps.
settings.softBlockAnnounceHint: HAPP in-app popup and banner on the browser page. Empty = first fake-location line is used.
settings.softBlockNameHint: Optional. Overrides the subscription profile title. Empty = keep normal title.
settings.happAdvancedHint: Fill in HAPP Provider ID in the subscription settings above to enable advanced HAPP features.
settings.happHideSettingsHint: Users cannot view or copy server connection details from the app.
settings.happNotifyExpireHint: Push notification 3 days before the subscription expires.
settings.happAlwaysHwidHint: User cannot disable HWID transmission in app settings.
settings.happHwidIntro: Limit how many physical devices a single subscription can be used on, by the x-hwid header sent by the client. Enforced at subscription fetch.
settings.happHwidExplainOff: Disabled. The panel does not track HWIDs and ignores the x-hwid header. No subscription-level device limit is enforced.
settings.happHwidExplainPermissive: Clients that send the x-hwid header are tracked and capped by maxDevices when fetching the subscription. Clients that do not send x-hwid receive the regular subscription and are not counted at fetch time.
settings.happHwidExplainStrict: Same as Soft, but clients without the x-hwid header are soft-blocked at subscription fetch: they receive a structurally valid subscription containing fake servers whose names are the “No HWID support” text below.
settings.happHwidExplainSoftBlock: When a client that sends x-hwid exceeds the device limit, it receives the same soft-block: a subscription with fake servers named after the “Limit reached” text. HAPP additionally shows an in-app popup. No 4xx/5xx is returned, so clients do not break.
settings.happHwidUpsertRateHint: Higher values shorten the cooldown before another DB upsert for the same HWID.
settings.happHwidNotSupportedRemark: Fake server names — no HWID support
settings.happHwidNotSupportedRemarkHint: Used in Hard mode for clients that do not send x-hwid. Each non-empty line becomes a separate fake server in the client UI. Up to 12 lines, 32 characters per line.
settings.happHwidMaxDevicesRemarkHint: Shown to any client whose device limit is reached. Each non-empty line becomes a separate fake server. Up to 12 lines, 32 characters per line.
settings.happHwidAnnounceHint: Sent as the HAPP `announce` header in addition to the fake server. HAPP shows it as an in-app popup. Max 300 characters. Non-ASCII is base64-encoded automatically.
settings.happPingTypeHint: How the app measures server latency.
settings.happPingUrlHint: URL used for proxy ping check. Only applies when ping method is Via Proxy.
settings.happColorProfileHint: Custom color theme JSON. Create a theme in the HAPP iOS app (long-press Appearance Theme), export to clipboard, then paste here.
settings.routingDesc: Configure which websites and services your users access directly (bypassing VPN) and which go through the VPN tunnel.
settings.routingEnabledHint: When disabled, subscriptions are generated without routing rules — all traffic goes through VPN.
settings.routingHowItWorksDesc:
Routing rules are embedded into subscription configs delivered to VPN clients. When a user opens a website or app, the client checks the destination against these rules:
• direct — traffic goes directly, bypassing the VPN (e.g. local banking, government services).
• block — traffic is dropped (e.g. ads, trackers).
• Everything else goes through the VPN tunnel as usual.

Rules also configure Split DNS: domains matching direct rules are resolved via the domestic DNS server, while all other queries go through the encrypted remote DNS.
settings.routingPresetsHint: Presets are additive — click multiple presets to combine them. For example, "Bypass RU" + "Block Ads" will add both rule sets. Duplicate rules are skipped automatically.
settings.routingRulesHint: Rules are applied top to bottom. First match wins. Disabled rules are skipped.
settings.routingNoRules: No rules yet. Add manually or pick a preset above.
settings.routingDnsHint: Domains matching "direct" rules are resolved via the domestic DNS. Everything else is resolved through the remote (encrypted) DNS via proxy tunnel.
settings.routingDnsDomesticHint: Plain UDP DNS for direct domains (e.g. Yandex DNS: 77.88.8.8)
settings.routingDnsRemoteHint: Encrypted DNS for proxied traffic (e.g. Cloudflare DoT: tls://1.1.1.1)
settings.routingClientSupportDesc:
Full support: HAPP (native routing protocol), Clash Meta / Stash (YAML rules).
Partial support: Hiddify / SFA / NekoBox (sing-box JSON — some clients may override rules with their own templates).
No support: v2rayNG, Streisand, Shadowrocket — these clients use URI subscriptions which cannot carry routing rules. Users need to configure routing manually.
settings.tabProbesDesc: External diagnostic agents that connect to nodes from the outside.

outbounds.title: Traffic Filtering
outbounds.pageDesc: Rules determine what to block, allow, or redirect through a proxy.
outbounds.resetDesc: Remove all rules, return to default
outbounds.rulesHint: One rule per line. Two built-in actions: reject(…) — block, direct(…) — allow through server. Rules apply top to bottom, first match wins.
outbounds.aclInlineDisabled: ACL inline editor is disabled: ACL is turned off in node settings.
outbounds.aclInlineDisabledFile: ACL inline editor is disabled: ACL source type is set to file mode in node settings.
outbounds.noProxyWarning: Proxy exists but no rules — proxy won't be used. Add a rule like:
outbounds.proxyChipsHint: Your proxies — click to insert into rule:
outbounds.defaultRulesWarning: If you set rules, server defaults (reject(geoip:cn), reject(geoip:private)) will be disabled. Add them manually if needed.
outbounds.proxyServersHint: for routing traffic through SOCKS5/HTTP proxy
outbounds.proxyDesc: Only needed if you want to route some traffic through your own proxy server. Add proxy here, then use its name in rules above: proxy_name(condition)

network.portConflictClientHint: This tunnel port is already used by another active link on the listening side.
network.modeReverseHint: Bridge initiates tunnel to Portal. Bridge can be behind NAT.
network.modeForwardHint: Portal connects to Bridge directly. All nodes need public IP.
network.confirmDeployChain: Deploy entire chain? This will sync all connected nodes in the correct order.
network.internetDesc: Traffic exits to the Internet from connected nodes

wizard.title: Setup Wizard
wizard.subtitle: Prepare the panel, the first nodes, and the initial access bundle in one guided flow.
wizard.scenarioHint: Select the deployment model that best matches your infrastructure. This only prepares the initial layout, and you can still add or change nodes later.
wizard.selfHostDesc: Install Hysteria 2 and / or Xray on the same server as the panel and prepare the starter access layout immediately.
wizard.remoteDesc: Use the panel as a control plane for proxy nodes running on separate VPS or dedicated servers.
wizard.selfHostHint: Choose the protocols to deploy, provide SSH access to the target server, and the wizard will prepare the starter group and first user automatically.
wizard.starterBundleDesc: The wizard will create a starter server group, attach the new nodes to it, and prepare the first VPN user admin so the subscription layout is ready immediately after deployment.
wizard.hysteriaChoiceDesc: High-performance UDP transport with QUIC and port hopping support.
wizard.xrayChoiceDesc: TCP transport with REALITY camouflage and managed runtime updates through the built-in agent.
wizard.hyDomainHint: Uses the panel domain. Hysteria shares the panel TLS certificate.
wizard.xrayPortHint: Port 443/tcp is used by the panel (Caddy). Xray defaults to 8443.
wizard.sshAccess: SSH access to the target server
wizard.sshAccessHint: Provide an address the panel can reach over SSH. Root access is recommended for unattended installation.
wizard.installing: Provisioning nodes, preparing starter access, and validating services. Please wait...
wizard.installPartial: Provisioning finished with errors. Fix the issue and retry setup, or continue manually.
wizard.streamError: Connection lost. Refresh to check status.
wizard.noProtocolSelected: Please select at least one protocol.
wizard.tooManyRequests: Too many requests. Try again later.
wizard.serverAddressRequired: Server IP or hostname is required
wizard.sshAuthRequired: SSH password or private key is required
wizard.credentialsDesc: Use this subscription link for the automatically prepared admin starter access.

migration.off: Legacy compatibility is OFF. Complete the wizard below to import users and arm the compat route.
migration.disableConfirm: Disable the Marzban compat route? Old links stop resolving until re-enabled.
migration.connectTitle: Connect to the source Marzban panel
migration.connectDesc: Provide the panel URL and the credentials of a sudo (or owning) admin. We never store these — they only live in this browser session until the import finishes.
migration.marzbanUrlHint: Include the protocol. Trailing slashes are stripped automatically.
migration.configureDesc: Choose which Celerity ServerGroup each Marzban admin's users land in, set the legacy subscription path, and paste the Marzban JWT secret so old links can be verified.
migration.pathHint: Must match the source panel's XRAY_SUBSCRIPTION_PATH. Default is sub. Reserved: api, panel, health, sse, docs, public, static.
migration.acceptSalt: Accept random URL salt (only if Marzban used XRAY_SUBSCRIPTION_URL_PREFIX with a *).
migration.jwtSecretPlaceholder: 64-char hex string from `SELECT secret_key FROM jwt;`
migration.jwtSecretHint: The command below runs inside the Marzban container and reads the secret through Marzban's own Python/SQLAlchemy layer. That makes it work with SQLite, MySQL, or any other database configured in the panel. Celerity stores the secret AES-encrypted.
migration.jwtSecretCommandTitle: Command to get the JWT secret
migration.jwtSecretCommandDesc: Run it on the server where Marzban is running. The command automatically finds the Marzban container by image or name.
migration.mappingDesc: Each Marzban admin's users join the chosen Celerity ServerGroup. The dropdown lists active groups only.
migration.fallbackGroup: Fallback ServerGroup (for users whose admin is unmapped)
migration.importVless: Re-use Marzban VLESS UUIDs (keeps Xray identity stable for users who already had VLESS).
migration.runDesc: Do not close this page until the import finishes — the task lives in panel memory and a restart will abort progress.
migration.finalizeDesc: Imported users are already in Celerity. The last step enables the /{path}/{token} route so old subscription links keep working.
migration.activateSuccess: Compat route armed. Old links should resolve now.

probes.title: External probes
probes.subtitle: Diagnostic agents that connect to your nodes like a regular client and report the result.
probes.disabledBanner: External probes are disabled. Enable them in settings.
probes.settingsIntro: A probe is a separate binary you install on your own server. It pulls a hidden subscription, runs sing-box and dials your nodes the way a client does.
probes.enableHint: While disabled, the panel accepts neither probe enrollment nor reports.
probes.installHint: Run this command on the server you want to check from. The token is single-use and expires in 24 hours.
probes.confirmRemove: Delete this probe together with its subscription and check history?
probes.scaleWarning: Probes times nodes times resources has grown large enough to load both the panel and the nodes noticeably.
probes.nodeSectionHint: What probes see when they connect to this node as a regular client. Every vantage point is shown separately, since a failure can also come from the probe's own uplink.
probes.sameHost: This probe runs on the node address, so its traffic never leaves the machine
probes.trafficLimitHint: Caps the hidden probe user. 0 means no limit.
probes.speedHint: Measurement spends real traffic on your nodes, so it is bounded per run and by a daily budget.
probes.speedEstimateLoad: A run pulls up to {size}. Every inbound is measured {runs} times a day, about {daily} of traffic from one probe.
probes.speedEstimateNoBudget: The daily budget covers {runs} runs, after which measurement pauses until the next day.
probes.speedEstimateCeiling: This size and time limit can measure up to {ceiling} Mbit/s. Anything faster fills the size cap first and is reported as "≥ {ceiling} Mbit/s" — raise the size to measure higher.
probes.targetsHint: One list for the whole panel: every resource is checked through every node. An unreachable resource usually means a geo-block or a blacklisted exit address.
probes.historyHint: Each segment is one check window. Ranges longer than 12 hours are shown as hourly rollups.
probes.historyEmpty: This probe has not reported any checks in the selected range.
probes.historyPending: The probe has not been installed yet, so there is nothing to show.
probes.truncated: More data than fits: only the end of the period is shown.
